::: {#rem-implied-for-all}
#### A conditional about a variable means "for all"

By convention, a conditional whose parts are predicates,
such as "if $x > 3$, then $x > 1$",
means the universal statement $\forall x, (x > 3 \Rightarrow x > 1)$,
even though no quantifier is written.
Mathematical statements leave out "for all" in this way all the time,
so put it back before deciding whether the statement is true.

:::
